Maria: Heads up — after switching a subset of nodes to kernel-v2 we saw a small but persistent p99 tail at ~150ms under multiplexed load. latency SLO is 120ms so this pushed a few routes over the limit. repro on perf lab with 32-concurrency synthetic workload. :thinking:
Aj: Which routes/models? can you paste the perf-ci job id?
Maria: perf-ci-bot/job/4721. Model is rdx-7b-quant, seq=512, KV cache enabled. interestingly p50/p95 unchanged, only p99 shifted. GPU util on canary nodes was 0.92 avg.
perf-ci-bot: job 4721 completed — artifacts at https://ci.redwood/perf/4721 :white_check_mark:
Sophia: did we change KV prefetch behavior in kernel-v2? iirc there was a small prefetch heuristic change to reduce memory churn.
Maria: yes, kernel-v2 switched to a conservative prefetch (mispredict avoidance). I profiled a run and observed more k/v misses at tail. log excerpt: ```kvcache: miss 0.18 -> 0.34 under burst windows; kv_prefetch: disabled for long-tail tokens```
Dmitri: That combination + sustained GPU util ~0.9 is a bad sweet spot: more kvcache misses -> more token recompute -> p99 jumps. We need to choose between reducing target_util or changing microbatching/admission.
Ethan: Agreed. Two principle knobs with minimal infra work: 1) soft-util cap (reduce target to ~0.8) 2) adaptive microbatch sizing that shrinks on p95 warming.
Aj: can we quantify cost vs latency for option 1 vs 2? i.e., how much throughput lost if we set target_gpu_util=0.8?
Sophia: Quick numbers from perf lab (same job): 
- util 0.92 -> throughput 1000 tok/s, p99 150ms
- util 0.82 -> throughput 880 tok/s, p99 115ms
- microbatch auto-shrink (min 1,max 8) with util unchanged -> throughput ~930 tok/s, p99 118ms
Dmitri: interesting. auto-shrink buys most of the latency without giving away full capacity. but need admission changes to shrink quickly on tail signal.
Maria: prototype admission config I tested: ```admission:
  strategy: slip-window
  slip_window_ms: 200
  target_gpu_util: 0.82
  p99_budget_ms: 120
microbatch:
  policy: adaptive
  min: 1
  max: 8
  shrink_trigger: p95_increase>20%```
Aj: what's slip-window? sounds new.
Dmitri: slip-window = allow short bursts above target but enforce soft backoff windows where we shed or shrink microbatches if p95/p99 degrades. basically smoother than immediate hard shed. reduces oscillation.
Sophia: we tested slip-window vs hard-cap in sim: slip-window had fewer request drops (0.2% vs 1.4%) and similar p99 improvements. code-level change is small (admission decision layer).
Ethan: Risk: some customers want maximum throughput; lowering target_util may be perceived as cutting performance. we should gate via rollout flags and per-tenant policy.
Maria: proposal: roll slip-window admission as opt-in canary for dedicated pools, default per-tenant setting to keep current util. we also add per-model microbatch hints in model config so model owners can choose conservative defaults.
Aj: sounds reasonable. action items: 1) Sophia/Dmitri to prepare a canary PR for admission layer + perf tests. 2) Maria to draft postmortem-style note listing kernel-v2 change and mitigation. 3) Ethan to update rollout docs and per-tenant flagging.
Dmitri: I'll also add a quick monitoring dashboard: p50/p95/p99, kvcache_miss_rate, gpu_util_softcap, microbatch_size distribution.
Sophia: I'll attach sim scripts to the PR. quick sim snippet: ```bash
./sim_load --model rdx-7b-quant --concurrency 32 --seq 512 --kvcache=on --admission=slip-window
```
deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated: kernel-v2 on pool-canary-17 at 1987654350
Maria: thanks all. we'll track for 24h and revert if any customer impact. :thumbsup:
Aj: TY. ping me if perf-ci shows regression on other models.
Ethan: +1, make sure to add a note for sales/customer success in case customers ask about perf variance.
